headline: Sherrill launches New Jersey housing plan, doubles state-land goal to 40,000 homes
dek: The five-pillar strategy pairs a larger public-land housing target with permit deadlines and a tax-credit auction as New Jersey says it needs 350,000 additional homes.
body: Gov. Mikie Sherrill unveiled a five-pillar housing strategy Tuesday in Atlantic City and announced immediate steps that would double New Jersey's planned housing production on state-owned land from 20,000 to 40,000 homes.

The plan was developed by the Housing Governing Council created under Sherrill's Executive Order 17. The governor's office says the council's report found New Jersey needs 350,000 additional homes to keep pace with growth, improve affordability and remain competitive.

The strategy calls for the state to examine underused public property, vacant offices and aging shopping centers for housing, with an emphasis on locations near transit, jobs and schools. The New Jersey Monitor reported that the council identified about 2,300 acres of state property and estimated the broader state-land program could support roughly 37,200 to 42,800 homes over time.

Sherrill also proposed a permitting 'shot clock' so applications move on clearer timelines and highlighted a dashboard tracking six projects that could produce more than 3,700 homes. Other announced actions include expanding hands-on assistance for municipalities and advancing transit-oriented developments in Red Bank, Bayonne and Linden.

The rollout includes a new state tax-credit auction intended to generate tens of millions of dollars for affordable housing. The administration said the broader strategy will also preserve existing affordable homes, expand homeownership opportunities and address unfair practices that can push rents higher; the announced housing totals are goals, not completed units.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Sherrill Unveils New Jersey Housing Strategy
seoDescription: New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill unveiled a housing plan that doubles the state-land goal to 40,000 homes and adds permitting and tax-credit measures.
sourceName: New Jersey Governor's Office; New Jersey Monitor
